# GENERATED by 08_Platform_Builds/build.py from 04_Agents/qc-reviewer v1.0.0. Do not edit; change the master and rebuild.

Standing instruction: Read the relevant skill from the EKOS Library before the work. Write a lesson card at the end of any project task.

To log a lesson, run: D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai local:<model> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"

Cards hold lessons and file paths only. No client data. No AI wording in deliverables.

## Agent definition

# QC Reviewer

## Role
Independent checker for drainage, H&H and civil deliverables. Works in its own context, separate from whoever
produced the work. Sees only the deliverables and the evidence files (native model output, plans, source studies,
agency letters). Never sees or relies on the producer's notes, chat, reasoning or checkpoint logs. Never edits a
deliverable; it writes a review record and, where asked, independent checks in 40_QC.

Always paired with report-writer: every report-writer hand-off ends here, and only this agent assigns item status.

## Inputs
- Mode: `full` | `submittal-audit` | `blind-rebuild` | `mock-agency`.
- Job number and job scope tags (e.g. `report-text tables exhibits hydrology flo2d fema pima-rfcd`).
- The deliverable set exactly as it will be (or was) transmitted: PDF/DOCX, zips as uploaded, response letter,
  comment matrix, model folders. For submittal audit: the archived upload package only.
- Evidence set: native program output, latest signed-sealed plans, source studies, governing manuals list,
  agency comment letters (all rounds), design discharge table, run register, decision register.
- Blind rebuild only: a source list (effective model and TDN, survey, approved plans, O&M, ESA) and a time box.
- Mock review only: governing manuals list and the review roles to play.

Not accepted as input: producer notes, AGENTS/continuation files of the producer, chat transcripts, the working
folders of the package (submittal audit), prior CLOMR products (blind rebuild).

## Outputs
All in `40_QC\<initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_qc_<mode>\` (Standard v0.3 layout, D56):
- `review_record.md` (+ `.xlsx` when more than about 40 items) from `templates/review_record.md`:
  one row per item with ID, document/page/section, finding, evidence (file + page), status, disposition,
  required action, owner. Status per D45: Addressed / Partial / Assumed / Not Addressed / Cannot Determine / Stale.
  Disposition (separate field): incorporated / superseded / no change.
- `decisions_for_JCO.md`: real decisions only, one per entry, with problem, options, consequences.
- Independent checks (scripts, workbooks, reruns) with a README stating which files are new. These stay in
  40_QC and never enter a deliverable (D30).
- Mode extras: package inventory CSV (submittal audit); judgment register, decision records and continuation state
  file (blind rebuild); merged mock-comment list (mock agency review); plan-report-calc crosswalk CSVs (when plans
  changed).
- Header line on every review output: "Internal QC record - not for transmittal. Review package is not stamped;
  JCO accepts or rejects each finding."

## Tools
- MCP library server (`get_skill`, `get_qc_rules`, `log_lesson`) or `library_cli.py` on EKOS.
- File read on the package and evidence; file write only inside its own 40_QC review folder.
- Shell on EKOS for zip listing, hashing, PDF text/annotation extraction (pypdf), DOCX/XLSX scans, and independent
  reruns of native programs on copies.
- Browser only for public reference lookups (FEMA NFHL, agency manuals) when the evidence set lacks a cited source.

## Skills it calls
| Skill | Used for |
|---|---|
| drainage-report-standard | assembly gate, folder map, numbering, PDF size and bookmarks (D52), open-items rules (D44) |
| drainage-report-build (+ addons/*.md) | report structure and jurisdiction add-on checks for the job |
| drainage-report-exhibit-standards | exhibit checklist when exhibit-reviewer has not already passed the set |
| agency-comment-response | comment log format, status vocabulary (D45), response wording |
| fema-clomr-lomr | FEMA package gate and AD-letter rules (submittal audit, blind rebuild) |
| impact-comparison | matched-model checks when a rise or dWSE claim is reviewed |
| pchydro-hydrographs, hechms-headless | native hydrology reruns for the native-vs-report table |
| hecras-2d-models, flo2d-model-runs | acceptance checks on 2D runs (volume, boundaries, build strings) |
| hy8-native-runs | native culvert reruns and HDS-5 independent check |
| swmm-ssa-storm-drain | independent storm drain recalculation |
| delivery-package-build | package manifest, checksums, zip content checks |

## Procedure

### 0. Set up (all modes)
1. Confirm separation: list what was received; refuse and remove from the review folder any producer notes,
   chat or checkpoint logs. Record the source of every file reviewed (path in the transmitted set, hash).
2. Pull the rules: `get_qc_rules('<tag>')` for every job scope tag, plus `package` and `comment-response` when a
   letter or package is in scope. Save the pulled rule list with the review record.
3. Confirm governing standards in a table: method, design storm set, HGL criterion, WQ, hydromodification, BMP
   siting (Placer), or FEMA guidance and effective model (FEMA). Load the matching drainage-report-build add-ons
   with `get_skill('drainage-report-build', resource='addons/<file>.md')`.

### 1. Full review (mode `full`)
1. Run the pulled QC rules over the PDF and its source folder: headings, traceability, tables, exhibits,
   appendices, software versions, existing infrastructure.
2. Native-vs-report table: every CP and return period, report Q vs native printout, max abs diff 0.0 cfs (D19).
   Every quoted hydraulic result maps to an output line (Q, HW, control type, barrel length, slope, velocity).
3. Design discharge traceability (HJR-C10): every Q in text, tables and captions matches the design discharge
   table (value, event, duration, source); one value per flow; qualifier (regional / local) on every reference;
   no recurrence interval outside the jurisdiction design set unless labelled sensitivity; caption storm = storm of
   the values shown; summary flow = flow used to size the structure.
4. Self-consistency (RPT-C09): datum check on every elevation table; summary tables pass the stated criteria;
   conclusions name only facilities and storms actually analyzed; every "incorporated in / see Section X" resolves
   to real content; sizes in report = plans = vendor calculators; appendix titles match contents and software;
   no files from other projects in the folder; latest sub-consultant batch used (diff against the final batch).
5. Run matrix: model x storm x RP x scenario from SUMMARY.OUT / HDF completion, not from the plan; check every
   narrative sentence naming storms, return periods or scenarios against it.
6. Plan-report-calc crosswalk when plans changed or the report cites a plan set (DSO-C08); see
   `reference/crosswalk_columns.md`. Every inlet, pipe and culvert in the latest plan set has a row with report and
   model values or a "not in report" flag; internal plan conflicts go to the designer as questions.
7. Independent recalculation where warranted: rerun separately and report each basis separately (corrected county
   method, calibrated SWMM, same files in SSA). Run every hydrology case for each plausible rainfall basis so the
   agency can choose without reruns. Stop or hand off every run this agent starts before the session ends.
8. Open items and assembly gate (D44): one internal open-items document exists; checklist rows resting on lidar
   culvert data, assumed bridge geometry, unknown layout or unconfirmed calibration are Partial or Assumed, never
   Addressed; deliverable text is in completed tense; no placeholder, DRAFT mark, highlight, markup layer, internal
   note or hold-until-final section in the transmittal set.

### 2. Submittal audit (mode `submittal-audit`) - before every FEMA resubmittal and after any closure or AD letter
1. Work only from the archived upload package (zips as uploaded) or the transmitted files, never working folders.
2. Inventory: list zip members with timestamps and sizes to CSV; flag outputs older than inputs, missing outputs,
   TMP files, header/build mismatches (FLOPRO.exe build = CONT.DAT line 1 = SUMMARY.OUT), missing zone/BFE
   shapefiles, boundary files that differ across duplicate effective / existing / proposed.
3. Classify every agency comment (all prior letters plus the closure letter): Addressed (with file + page evidence) /
   Partial (done but not run, or run but not reported) / Not Addressed / Stale (agency text repeated from a prior
   letter that the files disprove) / Cannot Determine; mark new comments as new.
4. Compare every response-letter and memo claim to the model output and GIS actually in the package; flag any claim
   without a file and page. Scan letter, matrix and report DOCX/XLSX for placeholders ([DATE], TBC, TO BE
   CONFIRMED, [ ], bracketed notes) and code fragments.
5. Rerun-all check: every model's output is newer than its last input edit, including existing conditions used
   for comparison.
6. Separate items that support a fee or reopen request (stale agency text, items already shown in the package)
   from legitimate findings. The cover letter may cite the stale items with file evidence; it does not argue.
7. Write build rules for the next package (what the package QC script must fail on).

### 3. Blind rebuild (mode `blind-rebuild`) - high-stakes CLOMR after several rebuilds only
1. Accept only the source list; prior CLOMR products are forbidden inputs.
2. Scope to the checks that matter: duplicate-effective reproduction, terrain and coordinate checks, native HY-8
   structure ratings, basin storage from the supplied grading surface, rise analysis.
3. Time-box to one session. Keep a continuation state file, a judgment register and decision records from the
   first hour; end the session with them current even if checks remain.
4. Compare findings with the main package and log every difference for JCO decision.

### 4. Mock agency review (mode `mock-agency`) - also the pre-QC self-check called by report-writer
1. Pre-QC self-check: run the draft through the pulled rules; zero open basic items (flow labels, return periods,
   numbering) before the draft goes to JCO.
2. Mock review: give the draft PDF, governing manuals list and review roles (town reviewer, county flood control
   reviewer, landowner-agency reviewer, public/opposition reader) to two independent reviewer instances on two
   different AI platforms (set A, set B) using `reference/mock_review_prompt.md`.
3. Each comment carries a unique source-prefixed ID (`A-TWN-01`, `B-FCD-03`), report location (section, page, table
   or figure), what is missing and the expected revision.
4. Merge: collapse duplicates, keep the stricter wording, record which set raised each item; overlap = priority.
5. Hand the merged list to the comment log (agency-comment-response) sorted into fix now vs carry to the next report.

### 5. Close (all modes)
1. Write `review_record.md` and `decisions_for_JCO.md`; set status per item (D45); leave disposition blank only
   where the producer has not yet responded (a blank disposition blocks issue).
2. Return the record to report-writer (or the producing agent) and JCO. Re-review only items whose evidence changed;
   mark items whose evidence predates the latest deliverable as Stale.
3. Learning log (below).

## Gotchas
- Mark the review package as a review record, not stamped; JCO must accept it (HOMEWOOD-005).
- Never overwrite designer originals; keep them in a reference folder and say so in the README (HOMEWOOD-005).
- Whole review plus 36 SWMM and 17 SSA runs took about 1.5 h scripted vs weeks of manual pipe-sizing iterations;
  scripted reruns are the main payoff (HOMEWOOD-005).
- Working response letter carried 10 TO BE CONFIRMED placeholders while the uploaded PDF stated those items
  complete; the agency reviewer cited letter-vs-model discrepancies (STARVALLEY-005).
- About a third of the agency closure text was stale wording from the prior letter; an audit with file evidence lets
  the cover letter say so without arguing (STARVALLEY-005).
- The audit must be done by an agent that did not build the package so it does not trust builder notes
  (STARVALLEY-005, HOMEWOOD-005).
- June package shipped outputs older than 16 edited inputs, a CONT.DAT build header that did not match SUMMARY.OUT,
  existing-condition folders with zero outputs, 8 TMP files and no zone shapefiles; FEMA closed the case and a new
  case and fee were required. FEMA runs the build-string comparison itself (STARVALLEY-004).
- Response sent 37 days early with unrun models and missing community letters; case closed for insufficient data
  (STARVALLEY-006).
- A full blind rebuild is too large for one pass: one session ran about 9.5 h and used 47 pct of the weekly
  allowance without producing the notebook or rise analysis (STARVALLEY-021).
- The blind rebuild found items the main package had not flagged: effective 24-hr storm model files absent (only
  3-hr supplied), basin grading storage 15.71 vs 18.10 ac-ft approved, a culvert headwater 0.02 ft over allowable,
  storm-drain outlet loss omitted (STARVALLEY-021, STARVALLEY-023).
- Three runs were left running unmonitored at session end; the reviewer must stop or hand off its own runs
  (STARVALLEY-021).
- Reviewer asked staff to catch basic errors (a 200-yr flow label) before review; 48 comments on a 5-page body cost
  a full rewrite cycle (SAHPARK-018).
- Both mock-review sets independently flagged the same core items (uniform Manning n, non-common mesh comparison,
  unsized detention, crossing language, preserve area not on maps); overlap confirmed priority (TANGERINE-001).
- ID collision: set A used A-1..A-3 for agency comments while set B used A-1..A-4 for the landowner-agency reviewer;
  prefix IDs by source set before merging (TANGERINE-001).
- Prompts written from a public or opposition view produce politically framed text; keep it internal and never
  paste it into a deliverable (TANGERINE-001).
- Final sub-consultant analysis arrived five weeks before the 30% DCR, yet only two numbers made it in, the exhibit
  placeholder was empty and the text claimed full incorporation; final images were 4-10x larger and sharper than
  preliminary (BARNETT-003).
- HGL table at about 1,580 ft vs plan datum near 6,240 ft; HGL above rim at one node (HOMEWOOD-015).
- Conclusion cited bioretention planters (none proposed) and the 10-yr storm while analysis was 50-yr 1-hr
  (HOMEWOOD-015).
- Appendix titled Hydraflow contained an SSA report; unrelated RETDET.xls in the storm folder (HOMEWOOD-015).
- Gallery sizes in vendor calculators (60-in / 18-in) differed from plans (72-in / 30-in) (HOMEWOOD-015).
- Design-basis summary in the 30% DCR reintroduced the regional/local ambiguity even though definitions existed;
  one flow quoted as 4,324 cfs and 4,325 cfs (BARNETT-006).
- Draft labelled a 100-yr value as 200-yr (source study has no 200-yr flows); inflow map captioned 10-yr showed
  100-yr rates; table referenced in text was missing; approach flow 2,673 cfs quoted as the crossing flow when the
  culvert was sized for 534 cfs (SAHPARK-003).
- Prior report stated the 500-yr basis two ways (NORTHLOOP-010).
- Old and new plan IDs shift (old SC11 = current SC15); keep both columns (VALENCIA-006).
- Plan sheets conflict internally (schedule vs profile labels; note says 3 arches while the sheet draws 2 barrels);
  record, do not pick silently (VALENCIA-006).
- A 387 ft profile length included a 50 ft segment past a junction; check dimensions before correcting lengths
  (VALENCIA-006).
- All 21 checklist rows were marked Addressed while the open-items memo listed 13 items that drive those rows
  (CALFIRE-016).
- A text-only export strips images; figure legibility, legends and graphic vintage are Cannot Determine until the
  native file is checked (BARNETT-001).

## Stop conditions
- Stop and report Cannot Determine (not a guess) when evidence for an item is missing from the set received.
- Stop the mode and ask JCO when the only material received is producer notes or working folders (submittal audit)
  or prior CLOMR products (blind rebuild).
- Blind rebuild: stop at the time box with state files current; never continue into a second unplanned session.
- Stop every model run this agent started, or hand it to model-run-supervisor with its status file, before ending.
- Never edit, rename, move or delete a deliverable or a producer original.

## Escalation (to JCO)
- Each real decision, one at a time: problem, options, consequences, plan/profile image where useful. Explain what a
  missing item is (model type, role) in the question.
- Any finding that changes a design flow, structure size, rise result or the FEMA case path.
- Differences between a blind rebuild or independent recalculation and the main package.
- Any request to transmit with items not Addressed (D44: compile is blocked unless JCO authorizes).

## Learning log
End every run with one lesson per new failure pattern found (not per item):
`log_lesson(project='<job no>', text='<pattern, check that caught it, rule tag>', evidence=['<40_QC path>'], source_ai='<platform>')`
or on EKOS without MCP:
`D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai <platform> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"`.
A recurring finding that has no QC rule yet is logged with "proposed rule:" and the redline/page it came from.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters QC-C01, QC-C02, RPT-C09, HJR-C10, DSO-C08 (plan-calc-crosswalk folded in as
  a module), with checks from QC-C03, QC-C04, QC-C06, QC-C07, RPT-C13, HJR-C21; decisions D19, D30, D44, D45, D52,
  D56. Items marked "default, to confirm": D52 bookmark set and 50 MB PDF target.

## Skill: drainage-report-standard v0.4.0

# Drainage Report Standard (workbook -> assemble -> post-process -> Word export -> compiled PDF)

Skill version 0.4.0. The package code on EKOS is still v0.3.0: the v0.4 changes in `reference/v0.4_change_spec.md`
are a spec, implemented and regression-tested in Phase 5. Until then this skill runs the v0.3 package and uses the
library helpers in `scripts/` (recalc, post-process, Word export, compile) where v0.4 will add package steps.
Do not edit the package code from this skill.

## When to use
- A drainage report, TM, addendum, H&H study, TDN or DCR is built on the Standard workbook (any jurisdiction).
- Kickoff or re-scope of a report: folder, Kickoff sheet, coordination plan, register seeding.
- Promoting, superseding, reconciling or auditing calcs; a design flow or basis value changed.
- Regenerating a draft after a calc, plan or comment change; compiling the submittal PDF.
- Content and formatting rules come from `drainage-report-build` and `drainage-report-exhibit-standards`; this skill
  is the mechanics of the Standard package. Memos: `drainage-technical-memo`. Comment cycles:
  `agency-comment-response`. Handover zips: `delivery-package-build`. New project folder and data:
  `project-intake`.

## Inputs
- Package root (EKOS): `D:\LocalAI_Test\Drainage_Report_Standard_v0.3_TRANSFER\Drainage_Report_Standard_v0.3_TRANSFER`.
  `<STANDARD>` = `<root>\standard\30_Standard_v0.3`. Map of files: `reference/package_map.md`.
- `%DOCS_PY%` = full path of the EKOS documents venv interpreter (openpyxl, python-docx, lxml, pypdf, pywin32)
  (D11). Set on EKOS as a user variable: `DOCS_PY=C:\EKOS\documents\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` (08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md).
  Never bare `python` or a global pip in a long job.
- `%SK%` = this skill's `scripts\` folder in the library.
- Job report folder `<Job>\ENGR\DOCS\Drainage Report\<ReportID>_<ShortName>\` and its workbook
  `00_Admin\<Job>_<ReportID>_Workbook.xlsx`.
- Stop and ask if missing: workbook path; milestone / revision / office address / contact in Setup (P-09..P-21);
  confirmed reviewing agency; JCO seal name and PE number (P-07/P-08).

## Steps

### A. Release check (every run)
1. Read `<STANDARD>\CURRENT.json`: `published: true`, note `standard_version`. On EKOS set `release_folder` to the
   EKOS path once (the shipped value points at an office OneDrive folder).
2. Workbook Setup S-41 and the template core-property version must equal CURRENT.json or the generator stops
   (`FAIL version gate`). A pre-v0.3 workbook is migrated with
   `"%DOCS_PY%" "<STANDARD>\build\patch_workbook_v03.py" <old.xlsx> <new.xlsx>`, never by hand; then register every
   existing calc (RECORD only if it was actually checked).
3. Never use `--allow-version-mismatch` for a job deliverable.

### B. Kickoff and folder (W00-W02)
4. Confirm the reviewing agency (City vs County) from the parcel record and the contract before drafting (HJR-C19);
   record the basis in Kickoff. Jurisdiction rules override this skill; load the `drainage-report-build` add-on.
5. Build the report folder with `make_report_folder.py` (command in `reference/governance_and_kickoff.md`), then add
   `30_Report\Issued\` beside `50_Correspondence\` and `00_Admin\DECISION_REGISTER.md` (D56, QC-C05; v0.3 does not
   create them). Dates in every folder and file name are YYYYMMDD (D56).
6. Fill Kickoff and Setup (S-01, S-03, S-04, S-06 flags, then the rest). Where the agency has a standard report
   outline (City of Tucson), its section list governs: keep every section and write "Intentionally left blank"
   with the reason where nothing applies; split existing conditions into hydrology and existing stormwater
   infrastructure (HJR-C19). In v0.3 do this with Narrative VERBATIM rows per section.
7. Set Setup S-36 to chapter-based numbering before any figure is rendered; figures and tables are numbered by
   section (Figure 4-1) (D52). Exhibit files `Fig<sec>-<n>_<Title>_<YYYYMMDD>.pdf`.
8. Plan: write `00_Admin\COORDINATION_PLAN.md` per the spec and seed CalcRegister / Narrative / ExhibitRegister
   (procedure and rules in `reference/governance_and_kickoff.md`). Stop for JCO approval of the plan.
9. Concept reports (channels with multi-use paths crossing roads, freeways or railroads; sites crossed by a large
   offsite wash) - put in the introduction, not deep in the body (HYD-C27):
   - whether the path is continuous under major crossings (freeway, railroad) or ends at them, and the crossing type
     at each road (at grade, under, con-arch);
   - for each existing crossing structure: stays, adequate, or replaced;
   - offsite conveyance alternatives with the count of road crossings for each; prefer one consolidated crossing;
     compare culvert cells for 10-yr vs 100-yr capacity;
   - alternatives note bank-protection options (e.g. geosynthetics on 4:1 vegetated slopes), precast vs
     cast-in-place culvert extensions, basin or spreader options at overchutes, terraced channel option (10-yr
     low-flow channel, 100-yr terrace outside sensitive areas);
   - flow paths described in downstream order;
   - written client decisions on level of protection (100-yr vs 500-yr), onsite containment and acceptance of
     controlled flooding; a designed overflow onto the site needs agency agreement;
   - grates/bar racks at fence crossings checked for headloss and debris; next deliverables listed after decisions.

### C. Governance during the work (W03-W05)
10. The ask creates the row: add the WORKING row before opening software. Work only in
    `20_Working\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_<Topic>\`. Promote with `promote_calc.py` (OPTION, or RECORD with checker
    initials). Actions PROMOTE / CASCADE / QC-TABLE / RECONCILE / PRECHECK: `reference/governance_and_kickoff.md`.
11. Decision register (QC-C05): when two values exist for one feature (design flow, structure size, basis) across
    tables, workbook and plans, list each with source, method and where used; classify isolated vs propagating;
    resolve isolated, evidence-backed ones and log them; ask JCO propagating ones one at a time (problem, options,
    consequences, plan/profile image). No table edit until decided. Once decided, update narrative, tables, exhibit
    labels, HY-8 and protection sizing together; keep each native run. Log in `00_Admin\DECISION_REGISTER.md`.
12. Design discharge traceability (HJR-C10): define regional and local storms and their peaks once in existing
    conditions and use the qualifier with every reference (10-yr regional, 100-yr local), no synonyms; keep a design
    discharge table (source cross section or culvert record ID, location, Q10, Q100, governing duration, use:
    crossing vs parallel flow); use only the jurisdiction's design recurrence intervals; restate the basis in the
    design section with the same wording and numbers; check every caption and table title against the storm of the
    values shown; summary flow = flow used to size the structure; allowable velocity is the velocity permitted over a
    lining or soil. v0.3 has no T-HYD-10 block: keep the table as T-HYD-04 rows plus a Narrative VERBATIM table
    lead-in, or in 40_QC as the check list.
13. Appendix calc rules (HYD-C26, D16, D38, D30, EXH-C13):
    - once plans show a selected design, run that design (size, count, inverts, length from plans, project-datum
      inverts, not an arbitrary 100 ft datum) and insert native output; drop option-comparison tables. Options still
      open: native sheets for each option, not only a summary;
    - licensed set (D16, default, to confirm): FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox, HY-8, Civil 3D hydraulic tools, HEC-RAS,
      HEC-HMS, FLO-2D, PC-Hydro. FlowMaster and CulvertMaster are legacy: reproduce legacy calcs in Toolbox / HY-8;
    - no new spreadsheet a reviewer must check; independent checks stay in 40_QC (D30);
    - print areas set so every output sheet plots on one page;
    - native output always in the appendix; an extracted or compact sheet may be added, titled "extracted summary",
      every value traced to the native file (D38);
    - Hydraulic Toolbox inlets: do not tick Add Profile; keep the native Word export as evidence; compact one-inlet
      page filled only from saved .hyd values; where the export prints longitudinal slope 0.0000, show the saved slope
      with a note that the native export misprints it; check every compact page visually.
14. Fill table blocks from RECORD printouts only; units in headers; one software version per analysis per cycle.

### D. Recalculate (D51)
15. Every time a script wrote to the workbook (and before any assembly):
    `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\xl_recalc.py" recalc --workbook "<wb>" --keep-copy "<wb>.pre_recalc.xlsx" --json "<..>\40_QC\recalc_<YYYYMMDD>.json"`
    Private Excel instance, events and link updates off, CalculateFullRebuild, then semantic compare. Require zero
    formula or input changes, zero new formula errors, and CalcRegister row-3 counters / Manifest J4 equal to what
    Excel shows. Work on an isolated workbook copy when testing; write only explicit input cells. Do not use the
    v0.3 `xl_recalc.ps1` (D12). LibreOffice recalc is a fallback only; flag it.

### E. Assemble (W06)
16. Run to a new dated file (issued drafts are never overwritten):
    ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "<STANDARD>\standard\assemble_report.py" ^
      --workbook "<..>\00_Admin\<Job>_<ReportID>_Workbook.xlsx" ^
      --template "<STANDARD>\Psomas_Drainage_Report_TEMPLATE.docx" ^
      --out "<..>\30_Report\Drafts\<Job>_<ReportID>_<Milestone>_<YYYYMMDD>_DRAFT.docx"
    ```
    `VERSION GATE FAILED` -> stop and report.
17. Read `_ASSEMBLY_REPORT.md`:
    - s1 must show OK version gate, OK verbatim narrative present unchanged, OK no engineer notes / context-only text
      printed. FAIL on CalcRegister (duplicate RECORD, RECORD without checker) blocks issue.
    - Issue gate (QC-C04; v0.4 CS-04 automates it): QC_Log Tier 1 answered > 0; CalcRegister populated for a design
      report; zero unregistered figures (every `[FIGURE:F-nn]` has an ExhibitRegister row); s3 VERIFY citations
      checked (prior study citation, current ADEQ CGP edition); a table referenced in two sections has one owner.
    - s5 unresolved placeholders -> list for the engineer; they stay yellow in Word (D44).
    - s9 human decisions grouped: governance first (duplicate RECORD, RECORD without checker, table rows citing
      non-RECORD calcs, narrative on excluded sections, ReportText withheld), then Manifest, text, data, derivations.
    - s10a rewrites: fill `proposed` in `_REWRITES.json` for each item (same numbers, names, cited standards; section
      tone; no new facts); show original -> proposed; record Accept / Revert / Edit (`final`); then
      `"%DOCS_PY%" "<STANDARD>\standard\apply_rewrites.py" --docx <draft> --rewrites <..>\_REWRITES.json`.
      Accepted wording that should persist goes back into the Narrative cell as VERBATIM. Not reviewable until s10a
      is empty.
    - s11 = calculation-of-record list for the transmittal.
18. Open items (D44): one internal QC open-items document in 40_QC (prerequisites table: jurisdiction, plans match
    analysis, T2 check, seal, waivers, open items; numbered open items typed geotechnical / final design / waiver /
    approval / JCO decision / submittal; native-vs-report calc cross-check table; standards checklist with status and
    location, deviations called out; empty markup response log). Every assembly WARN, unresolved placeholder and
    human decision is closed or listed there. Checklist status uses Addressed / Partial / Assumed / Not Addressed /
    Cannot Determine / Stale (D45); rows resting on lidar culvert data, assumed bridge geometry, unknown layout or
    unconfirmed calibration are Partial or Assumed. Deviations from the Standard (tool version, exhibit method,
    missing template) are listed as JCO decisions. Deliverables read in completed tense; the open-items document is
    never transmitted.

### F. Post-process the DOCX
19. ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\postprocess_docx.py" --docx <draft.docx> --fix --out <draft>_PP.docx --preparer "Psomas (JCO)" --json <..>\40_QC\postprocess_<YYYYMMDD>.json
    ```
    Sets author / last-modified-by to the firm string, clears comments/keywords/subject, drops template custom
    properties, removes DATE fields from headers and footers. It lists, and never deletes, placeholders, leftover
    `[FIGURE:]` / `[TABLE:]` / `[LIB:]` slots and rewrite tags (D44: placeholders stay flagged until the assembly
    report shows them closed). Remove template paragraphs that do not apply and slots of excluded sections by hand
    or by regenerating; set cover office address and project number in Setup and regenerate.
20. Fix every finding at its source (workbook, Narrative, template), regenerate, and re-run. Tables: thin borders on
    all cells, header row in the template header style, no alternating shading (D47, default, to confirm); one
    caption per table above it, numbered by section, no second title inside the table; header row repeats; cells
    centered; portrait and full width (drop constant columns and note them); native Word tables, never screenshots;
    elevations 2 decimals without thousands separator, discharges whole cfs, one precision per column; each table
    introduced by a "presented in Table n" sentence; fit to one page where possible (RPT-C06).
    Page breaks only before main sections and appendices; template styles for headings and spacing, no manual
    returns; references numbered 1), 2) with real sources only; directions abbreviated with a period (S.) or road
    names written out, one convention; no dates in footers; fix TOC tab alignment and stray characters (pull a fresh
    template if unsure); cover carries a project site photo, preferably from the field visit (RPT-C06).
21. Figures embedded in the docx are downsampled to 200-300 dpi at print size before insertion.

### G. Word export
22. ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\word_export.py" --docx <draft>_PP.docx --pdf <..>\30_Report\Drafts\<name>.pdf --email-pdf <..>\<name>_email.pdf
    ```
    Separate Word instance; fields, TOC and tables of figures updated twice; PDF with heading bookmarks. Then
    confirm no paragraph lacks a named style and every Table/Figure number resolved (LibreOffice previews show
    "Table Introduction-1" where Word shows "Table 1-1": judge captions in Word).
23. Render every page and look at each one (`pdftoppm -r 45 -png <pdf> <prefix>`, contact sheets 5x2) before
    issue: cover on one page, footer not on 11x17 figure pages, no large white areas, no orphaned headings.

### H. Compile the bookmarked PDF (W09)
24. Write `30_Report\compile_manifest.json` (format in the script docstring) from the newest editable source and its
    fresh Word export: body split at the end of each main section with that section's 11x17 figures inserted, one
    divider per appendix and per plan set or study, native output (PC-Hydro printouts and hydrographs per CP, HEC-HMS
    output, Atlas 14 PFDS printout, HY-8 report, RAS computation summaries, FIS/LOMR/dam-safety pages), landscape
    pages rotated. Never hardcode page numbers in prose.
25. Prepare sources: highlight the relevant Q values in reference studies; replace table numbers on images with markup
    matching size, font and color; flatten author markups in the PDF reader (originals kept); third-party FreeText
    (e.g. LOMR pages) flattened or noted; inherited plan revision clouds removed from the compiled copy, original
    marked PDFs kept (D48).
26. ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\compile_pdf.py" build --manifest <..>\30_Report\compile_manifest.json --split
    ```
    Required bookmarks (D52, default, to confirm): cover, TOC, each main section, each appendix, each exhibit; children
    sorted by page. Checks: every bookmark and link target resolves, links dropped by the compile fail, page-by-page
    source comparison in the QA JSON (keep it in 40_QC), near-blank pages, size against S-35.1 / the agency limit
    (D52: 50 MB per file or the agency limit if lower; over -> compress, then split at top-level bookmarks; keep a
    reduced copy for transfer).
27. Placeholder pages only for named future items, labelled with the item; no blank areas in the body; remove
    unneeded pages, unrequested appendices and review-draft wording (D50).
28. Final interactive check of bookmarks and links in a native PDF reader (Bluebeam), not a browser viewer.
29. A pending model rerun: hand the watcher (wait for the new HDF, regenerate results and figures, recompile, copy to
    10_Record) to `model-run-supervisor`.

### I. Issue (W10) and after
30. Gate: open-items document empty, or JCO authorization recorded and the unresolved items listed in a separate
    internal document (D44); PRECHECK pass; RevisionLog row for the milestone; T1 complete, then T2 and T3.
31. Issued set in `30_Report\Issued\<YYYYMMDD>_<Milestone>\` with RECORD_SET.md (final PDF, frozen docx, transmittal).
    Handover package -> `delivery-package-build` (into 30_Report/Issued). Comments back -> `agency-comment-response`.
32. Design change after issue: log it in REVISION_LOG.md with affected letters, figures, tables and sections; CASCADE
    for hydrology changes; re-run in a new 20_Working folder; promote; regenerate to a new dated draft; compare old vs
    new drafts (Word Compare or `pandoc -t markdown` + diff) and the two assembly reports; T2 reopens for changed
    letters, T3 for changed sections; recompile.
33. Text that belongs in every future report goes into the library JSON (v0.4 release work), never into one .docx;
    project prose goes into Narrative or CalcRegister ReportText so regeneration reproduces it.

### J. End-to-end rerun of a job (DSO-C14)
34. Parameterize the project root and job work folder in every script (one parameter file); grep for absolute paths
    before a rerun - none outside the parameter file. Scripts write `.log` and `.err`; dated scripts folder
    `20_Working\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_scripts\` (D56 replaces 99_Working).
35. Prerequisites: .hy8 writer module, minimal HMS template project, Report_Template_7 and memo template paths, pinned
    ras_commander, pywinauto, HY-8 8.00, HEC-HMS 4.13 (D01), HEC-RAS 6.6 (D02). Fix known blocking items from the
    prior run first.
36. Run order: due diligence; data/GIS (DEM, subbasins, culverts, terrain compare, crossings, inventory); hydrology
    (HMS build/runs, PC-Hydro, routing); 1D/2D runs in a separate agent; HY-8; alternatives; exhibits; report
    (recalc, assemble, post-process, Word export, contact sheets); compile; record copy. FLO-2D and HEC-RAS in
    parallel on separate core sets (D06 limits on EKOS).
37. Budget wall time: about 6.5 h for a one-session preliminary report; about 48 h minimum for a full 2D pilot,
    governed by HEC-RAS (10 plans about 43 h sequential on 12 cores); report build about 3 min per rebuild.
38. Every edit script is idempotent: back up first, check whether an insert already exists, assert counts before
    writing. After a JCO change edit the builder inputs first; do not run stale downstream builders.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
- Load `get_skill("drainage-report-build", resource="addons/<file>.md")` for the reviewing agency before step 6.
- `addons/city-of-tucson.md`: City manual outline is the section list (HJR-C19).
- `addons/town-of-marana.md`: concept reports explain trail termination or the crossing at I-10/UPRR (HYD-C27);
  regional vs local terminology per MDM 4.1 (HJR-C10, D24).
- `addons/town-of-sahuarita.md` / `addons/pima-county-rfcd.md`: a designed overflow onto the site conflicts with
  matching existing peak Q and floodplain at the property boundary (HYD-C27); 10-yr and 100-yr are the design events
  (HJR-C10).
- `addons/fema.md`: TDN behaviour via S-02.

## Gotchas
- openpyxl reads stale values for formula cells unless the workbook was recalculated and saved by Excel (SAH-012).
- A library-written workbook showed a COUNTIF wildcard counter of -14 status issues; native recalc gave 0 with no
  formula change (EKOS-LOCAL-018).
- Native Excel merges adjacent validation ranges and drops default styles; compare semantics, not raw XML
  (EKOS-LOCAL-018).
- Learning the workbook layout took four inspection passes plus manifest and library dumps; keep a named-range map per
  Standard version (SAH-012).
- Compiled PDF was 23.8 MB; a 3.4 MB compressed copy was needed for transfer (SAH-012).
- Figures first numbered 1-7, then renumbered by section, so every exhibit was rendered twice (CALFIRE-013).
- The memo template ships its own core.xml and duplicated parts (CALFIRE-013).
- TOC level-2 tab leader missing in the template on short entries (CALFIRE-013).
- Cover office address and project number were placeholders (CALFIRE-013).
- Generated DOCX was 49-56 MB with 12 full-resolution images; some paragraphs had no style and python-docx failed on
  them; Word cleanup took 46 saves over about 1.6 h on submittal day (TANGERINE-011).
- Issued 96-page PDF and all three exhibit PDFs had no bookmarks (TANGERINE-011, TANGERINE-016).
- First template pass pushed the cover to 2 pages and ran the footer across the 11x17 figure page (VALENCIA-009).
- An integration script wrote the body then failed an assertion; rerunning would duplicate a paragraph - fix and
  resume (VALENCIA-009).
- Compact output used pageBreakBefore, not w:br; grouping logic must handle both (VALENCIA-009).
- All four reports of one program were first built in a generic layout and restructured with one-time patches, about
  1.25 h rework; build to the standard from the first draft (RKN-014).
- Table with green highlights, mixed elevation decimals and a table name not matching the caption (SAHPARK-004).
- A screenshot of an Excel table plotted poorly; tables are native Word tables (SAHPARK-004).
- A short appendix table ran onto a second page (SAHPARK-004).
- Excessive and inconsistent spacing between sections; a large blank area on one page (SAHPARK-005, TANGERINE-018).
- Table mismatch flagged twice, extra space three times, a stray bracket and footer dates in one draft (TANGERINE-018).
- Appendix bookmark order wrong (Table A-2 on p. 26 listed after Table A-1 on p. 27) (CALFIRE-014).
- Source LOMR pages bring FreeText annotations into the compiled PDF (CALFIRE-014).
- A report link did not work in the reviewed draft (CAMPBELL-020).
- Source PDFs raise pypdf "Multiple definitions for key /PageMode" warnings; harmless (RKN-015).
- Compiled PDFs reached 55-86 MB and 700 MB-1 GB (RKN-015, VALENCIA-008).
- Revision cloud annotations vanished in merged plan pages; 39 sheets had to be re-rendered (VALENCIA-008).
- The final report must not carry plan revision clouds (VALENCIA-008).
- The editable Word body held corrections that never reached its PDF; compile from the newest source and its fresh
  export (VALENCIA-008).
- Browser-based reader checks failed under computer-use URL policy; use a native PDF reader (VALENCIA-008).
- Deviations from the Standard (HEC-HMS 4.13 vs 4.12, Python exhibits vs QGIS, missing brand template) must be listed
  as JCO decisions, not buried (RKN-018).
- All 21 checklist rows were marked Addressed while the open-items memo listed 13 items, including culvert
  size/inverts, bridge low chord and new impervious area that drive those rows (CALFIRE-016).
- A 30% draft went out with QC_Log 0/27, CalcRegister empty, 6 unresolved placeholders (seal PE number, prior study
  fields) and F-06/F-08 unregistered (SAH-013).
- The assembler flagged library id PROJECT-TEXT not found and treats PROJECT-TEXT as one entry per report (later
  sections duplicate); put project text through the Narrative sheet until CS-03 ships (SAH-013).
- The s60 post-process deleted leftover placeholder paragraphs, hiding open items in the docx; keep them listed in the
  assembly report (SAH-013).
- An agent team changed a design flow from 886.6 to 823.1 cfs; JCO reversed it: 886.6 cfs is the larger area routed to
  the crossing (CAMPBELL-014).
- One structure (D1) changed three times (3 arches, 2-18 in pipes, 2-24 in pipes); keep each native run and the final
  decision (VALENCIA-011).
- JCO wanted downstream flows to match the updated pavement drainage maps, not recomputed totals (VALENCIA-011).
- Do not call an odd size a typo without evidence; 18x11 in is a standard concrete arch (VALENCIA-011).
- Do not put JCO working assumptions (e.g. utility conflicts mitigated) in report text unless told (VALENCIA-011).
- A draft appendix had only an options summary table on an arbitrary datum while the plans already showed a
  3 - 10x4 ft RCBC (SAHPARK-012).
- Custom normal-depth spreadsheets with an undocumented geometry sketch added review time and were removed
  (SAHPARK-013).
- FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox 5.5 native Word export prints longitudinal slope 0.0000 although the saved input and dialog
  have a nonzero slope; reproducible across 110 cases (VALENCIA-002).
- Raw Toolbox output took 2 pages per inlet; reformatting in Word from native values was accepted by JCO
  (VALENCIA-002).
- The reviewer read 41 of 48 pages before learning the path was claimed continuous under I-10 and UPRR; Development
  Engineering asked for the trail to stop at I-10 or explain the crossing (BARNETT-011).
- A designed overflow onto the site creates a second floodplain path and conflicts with matching existing peak Q and
  floodplain at the property boundary; needs Town and PCRFCD buy-in (PHXZOO-005).
- Double chain-link fencing passes stormwater freely, which removed the pipe-escape concern only because no pipes leave
  the enclosures (PHXZOO-005).
- The design-basis summary sentence in a 30% DCR reintroduced the ambiguity flagged earlier even though definitions
  existed (BARNETT-006).
- One flow quoted as 4,324 cfs and 4,325 cfs in different places (BARNETT-006).
- A draft labeled a 100-yr value as 200-yr; the source study has no 200-yr flows (SAHPARK-003).
- An inflow map captioned 10-yr showed 100-yr rates (SAHPARK-003).
- Missing table referenced in hydrology text (SAHPARK-003).
- Approach flow (2,673 cfs) quoted as the crossing flow when the culvert was sized for 534 cfs (SAHPARK-003).
- A prior report stated the 500-yr basis two ways (NORTHLOOP-010).
- A draft did not follow the City outline; restructure requested and all City sections required even when empty
  (TANGERINE-017).
- Jurisdiction unclear (City vs County); a second reviewer noted contracts and the parcel map point to County
  (TANGERINE-017).
- Scripts held hard paths to another project folder and to Python 3.12 site-packages; all scripts hard-coded the
  OneDrive job folder and the D: work folder (CALFIRE-018, SAH-018).
- Model runs and web services are the waits (CALFIRE-018).
- The original pilot run used about 25 h of continuous agent time plus 43 h of RAS queue (SAH-018).
- Fix SAH-002, SAH-003, SAH-006 and SAH-015 items first or the same reruns repeat (SAH-018).
- Recorded run times (FLO-2D UPPER + LOWER, h): 3-hr 100-yr 0.63 + 0.82; 24-hr 100-yr 1.86 + 2.91; 3-hr NoBerm
  0.34 + 0.69; 24-hr NoBerm 1.09 + 3.54; 3-hr NoBerm MineFill 0.33 + 0.69; other frequencies est. 1.5 h per pair;
  HMS 50 runs about 40 min; PC-Hydro 67 subbasins 25 min; report build about 3 min (SAH-018).
- First delivery package used a non-standard folder name and missed printouts/QC; rebuilt two hours later
  (RKN-019) - see `delivery-package-build`.
- Download links failed on the phone and email was not set up; OneDrive on the phone worked (CAMPBELL-023).

## QC checks
- Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('report-text')`, `get_qc_rules('tables')`, `get_qc_rules('appendix')`,
  `get_qc_rules('package')`, `get_qc_rules('exhibits')`, plus the jurisdiction tag (`pima-rfcd`, `tucson`,
  `marana`, `sahuarita`, `fema`, `placer`, `caltrans`).
- Recalc: zero new formula errors; register counters match Excel (EKOS-LOCAL-018).
- Assembly: s1 OK lines; issue gate (T1 > 0, CalcRegister populated, zero unregistered figures, VERIFY cited); s10a
  empty; open-items document empty or JCO authorization recorded.
- DOCX: no unstyled paragraphs; no leftover slots in included sections; no DATE fields in footers; properties set to
  the firm; no tool or assistant names; tables thin-bordered without banding (SAH-012, TANGERINE-011, CALFIRE-013).
- Every page rendered and viewed (SAH-012, CALFIRE-013, VALENCIA-009).
- Compiled PDF: minimum bookmark set present and ordered by page; every bookmark and link resolves; QA JSON page
  comparison clean; no revision clouds, no review-draft wording, no unflattened stray annotations; size under the
  agency limit (TANGERINE-016, CAMPBELL-020, CALFIRE-014, VALENCIA-008, RKN-015).
- Every Q in text, tables and captions matches the design discharge table (value, event, duration, source); no
  recurrence interval outside the jurisdiction design set unless stated as a sensitivity (HJR-C10).
- No change to a design flow or structure size in tables without a decision-register entry; decided values identical
  across narrative, tables, exhibits, HY-8 and protection sizing (QC-C05).
- Section list matches the agency outline one to one where one exists (HJR-C19).
- Appendix: native output for the selected design; extracted summaries labelled and traced; Toolbox slope note where
  the export shows 0.0000; 100% compact-page visual check logged (HYD-C26, EXH-C13).
- Rerun: grep for absolute paths before a rerun; none outside the parameter file (DSO-C14).

## Skill: drainage-report-build v2.0.0

# Drainage Report Build

## When to use
Any drainage report, TM, DCR or memo build, and any revision from a JCO markup or agency comments. This skill is the entry
point: it sets the order of work and the rules every report must meet, then hands each task to the skill or agent that owns
it. Jurisdiction rules (from the add-on) override anything here; decisions D01-D57 override older rules.

Who does what:
| Task | Owner |
|---|---|
| Assembly chain (workbook -> assemble_report.py -> post-process -> Word export -> compiled PDF) | `drainage-report-standard` |
| Exhibit sheet standards (sizes, ramps, base content, FIRM marking, text size) | `drainage-report-exhibit-standards` |
| Scripted exhibit series | `scripted-exhibit-sheets` |
| Writing narrative and tables | agent `report-writer`, always paired with agent `qc-reviewer` |
| Independent review, submittal audit, blind rebuild | agent `qc-reviewer` |
| Exhibit review | agent `exhibit-reviewer` |
| Prior studies, criteria research, jurisdiction confirmation | agent `due-diligence-researcher` |
| Long model runs, queues, rerun-all gate | agent `model-run-supervisor` |
| PC-Hydro | `pchydro-hydrographs` |
| HEC-HMS | `hechms-headless` |
| HEC-RAS 2D | `hecras-2d-models`; result rasters `hecras-result-rasters` |
| FLO-2D | `flo2d-model-runs` |
| HY-8 culverts | `hy8-native-runs`; legacy calc reruns agent `legacy-calc-reproduction` |
| Storm drain SWMM / SSA | `swmm-ssa-storm-drain` |
| Existing vs proposed comparison, rise maps | `impact-comparison` |
| FEMA CLOMR / LOMR packages and AD responses | `fema-clomr-lomr` |
| Groundwater reinfiltration | `groundwater-reinfiltration-sizing` |
| Letter or technical memo format | `drainage-technical-memo` |
| Agency comment-response log | `agency-comment-response` |
| Project intake, terrain, CRS log | `project-intake` |
| CAD base reissue | `cad-base-update` |
| Delivery package | `delivery-package-build` |
| Closeout lessons | `project-harvest` |

## Inputs
- Job folder in the Standard v0.3 layout (D56): 00_Admin, 01_Reference, 02_Data, 10_Record, 20_Working, 30_Report, 40_QC,
  50_Correspondence (issued sets in 30_Report/Issued); dates YYYYMMDD. If the job is not in this layout, run `project-intake` first.
- Scope / contract, parcel record and plat case, current plan set, survey, geotech report.
- The Standard workbook for the report (00_Admin) when the job uses the Standard.
- Prior studies and effective FEMA data (from `due-diligence-researcher`).
- For revisions: the marked-up PDF (JCO or agency) and the current editable source.

## Steps

### 0. Start: jurisdiction, governing manuals, method selection
1. Confirm the jurisdiction and the reviewing agency from the parcel record, plat case, GIS jurisdiction layer and the
   contract before choosing any manual. Where City vs County or Town vs County is unclear, record both readings and ask
   JCO. Flag any conflict with the project description.
2. Load the add-on(s) for that jurisdiction (table under Jurisdiction add-ons). More than one can apply (for example
   town-of-marana + fema).
3. Cite the current edition of each governing manual from the add-on; never cite a superseded document; cite the current
   version of any redone prior study. Keep the governing policies and program guides in `01_Reference\Agency` for citation.
4. Use the agency report outline as the section list when the agency publishes one. Keep every section; where nothing
   applies write "Intentionally left blank" with the reason.
5. Method selection (write it into the design-basis section and the workbook Setup):
   - hydrology method by watershed size and jurisdiction (add-on method table);
   - rainfall source, statistic, return period and duration;
   - design events for each system type (only the jurisdiction design set; anything else is labelled a sensitivity);
   - hydraulic tools from the licensed set (D16): FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox, HY-8, Civil 3D hydraulic tools, HEC-RAS 6.6,
     HEC-HMS 4.13, FLO-2D, PC-Hydro. FlowMaster and CulvertMaster are legacy (default, to confirm).
   - tabulate concentration points with method, area and design Q.
6. If the scope adopts published regional or effective hydrology instead of new hydrology:
   - read the agency supersession memo first and confirm which study governs at the site (study limits);
   - take Q10 / Q100 from the governing tables and state which engine's results are used where several are tabulated;
   - for an effective FEMA study read the TDN storm list and controlling-storm statement and confirm the package holds the
     rainfall-runoff model and inputs for every storm case; request missing cases before modelling;
   - an event outside the published set (for example 500-yr) needs written client agreement to a ratio method or is scoped
     as added service;
   - apply the study's technical guidance (mesh size etc.) to any new model; represent existing flow splits (berm
     breakouts) rather than assuming containment.
7. Plan deficiencies: where the design differs from or falls short of the current plan set, list each item and ask JCO how
   to handle it (revise plans, note in report, alternative design). Never assume plan revisions.
8. Open the one internal QC open-items document for the report in 40_QC (D44). Every assumption, decision item and
   missing input goes there, not into the deliverable text.
9. For a markup revision:
   - read the markup page by page (Bluebeam annotations) and build a response-log row for every comment
     (`agency-comment-response`; status per D45: Addressed / Partial / Assumed / Not Addressed / Cannot Determine / Stale;
     disposition in a separate field: incorporated / superseded / no change);
   - copy the marked-up PDF to the 40_QC T3 review folder as `<Job>_<ReportID>_<Milestone>_<YYYYMMDD>_JCO-Markup.pdf`;
   - edit builder inputs first, then rebuild; never run stale downstream builders.

### 1. Design basis and discharge traceability
1. Define each storm used (regional and local, design and FEMA) once, in existing conditions. Use the qualifier with every
   reference ("10-yr regional", "100-yr local"); no synonyms.
2. Build a design discharge table: source (cross section, culvert record or CP id), location, Q10, Q100, governing
   duration, use (crossing vs parallel flow), method. Every Q in text, tables and captions matches it: one value, one
   qualifier, one source per flow.
3. Restate the design basis in the design section with the same wording and numbers. Keep the summary flow equal to the flow
   that sized the structure (approach flow is not crossing flow).
4. Check every map caption and table title against the storm of the values shown.
5. Allowable velocity is the velocity permitted over a lining or soil, not "the velocity of the soil".
6. Critical facilities (substation, BESS, utility, emergency facility) and any site needing a 500-yr WSE (D22):
   - confirm the critical-facility designation and requirement with the jurisdiction (improvements above the 500-yr WSE
     plus any freeboard from the add-on);
   - 500-yr WSE source, in this order: FIS 0.2% profile only where its cross sections bracket the site (annotate the profile
     with project extents and values used); else agency 500-yr hydrology; else a documented provisional value with agency
     agreement. A 1.75 x Q100 ordinate scaling is a labelled sensitivity only. Zone AO depth is not an elevation;
   - state the 500-yr source once; tabulate floor, pad and equipment elevations with datum and the controlling 100-yr and
     500-yr WSE;
   - add a FEMA floodplain section: effective zones, floodway, BFEs, how they constrain the design, and the consequence if
     existing ground is below the 500-yr WSE.
7. Rise and impact thresholds are cited from the governing agency or stakeholder per project (D29); no hard-coded 0.1 ft.
   Comparisons use `impact-comparison`.

### 2. Content rules
Watersheds and hydrology
1. Onsite watersheds end at the property line; omit offsite areas draining away; existing and proposed totals match to
   two decimals. Set the onsite boundary at the project boundary so pre vs post is shown there.
2. Areas not regraded are modelled on existing contours.
3. Nested areas: list each catchment with its parent; run a total-area unattenuated case once; never add upstream basin
   outflows or pipe catchment flows to it. Where detention is modelled, route the upstream outflow and add only the
   incremental downstream area. Load soils and attributes by the same catchment key as geometry; stop on mismatched keys.
4. Offsite areas near a storm drain: bring in the storm drain, manholes and inlets; include roadway and upstream
   subdivision areas tributary to it; state the inlet capture assumption; label upstream offsite infrastructure.
5. Watershed exhibits: boundaries follow visible ridge lines on shown topo; flow arrows agree with contours; Tc path shown;
   "flowline" where no stream exists (contour intervals per `drainage-report-exhibit-standards`, D42).
6. Tc = hydrology program value (PC-Hydro 5-min minimum); never call time to peak Tc; table values match native output.
7. Percent impervious and cover need a stated source (plans, independently labelled imagery meeting a set acceptance, or a
   named cover scenario S1/S2/S3). Classifier output is not field truth.
8. Basin outlets not surveyed: search as-builts and GIS pipe layers first; else ask the owner once and store the answer as
   a versioned scenario (source = owner); supersede explicitly, never overwrite; flag implausible derived slopes. Fallback
   with no invert data: pipe from lidar with 1 ft minimum cover tied to outfall ground.
9. Rainfall tables state source, statistic, return period and duration; runoff-coefficient columns headed with the symbol
   (for example Cw) and plain numbers.

Detention, first flush, infiltration
10. Give preliminary pre vs post peak Q and storage estimates even at concept level. Preliminary detention where PR > EX
    (2, 10, 100-yr): Vs = Vin,PR x (1 - Qex / Qpr), max of the three events; replace with a routed design at final.
11. Keep flood detention, first flush / water quality, sediment storage and harvesting separate, each with its own
    criteria and maintenance. Distributed (pod-level) detention gets a ledger per pod: allowable Q, required volume,
    phasing trigger, responsible entity. Name maintenance access and the responsible entity.
12. First flush retained below the outlet invert (raise the outlet inlet rather than regrade the basin); shallow first-flush
    areas up to 9 in deep where needed. Model outlets exactly as drawn.
13. Drawdown = retained depth / design infiltration rate with the standard factor of safety. Untested rate (D23): state the
    basis used and that field testing is required; the add-on sets the method (Pima: required-rate method; Placer: half
    NRCS rate with 0 in/hr sensitivity).
14. Flag basins in mapped riparian habitat and outfalls direct to a major wash (detention waiver candidates).
15. Maintenance / inspection plan only if the jurisdiction requires it; otherwise ask JCO.

Channels, culverts, streets
16. Constructed unlined earthen channels n = 0.025; natural channels from land cover with the source cited (D27). Tables
    show required depth (normal depth + required freeboard) vs provided, and the lining (earthen / unlined, concrete,
    shotcrete, riprap
